title: How health conditions change what you eat
rule: Some conditions change nutrient targets or how you should eat them. Handled adjusts the plan where public health sources are clear, and otherwise says what to ask your care team. It never sets targets for kidney disease, and it does not show calorie numbers to someone with an eating disorder history.

anemia.label: Iron-deficiency anemia
anemia.note: Eat iron foods with vitamin C, and keep coffee, tea and calcium away from those meals. Iron pills need a dose and a recheck from your doctor.

diabetes.label: Diabetes or prediabetes
diabetes.note: Keep carbs steady from meal to meal and favor high-fiber carbs. If you take insulin or a sulfonylurea, change your carbs only with your care team.
diabetes.confirm_with: your doctor or a diabetes educator

hypertension.label: High blood pressure
hypertension.note: The DASH pattern (vegetables, fruit, beans, low-fat dairy) lowers blood pressure. The American Heart Association's ideal is 1,500 mg of sodium a day.

cholesterol.label: High cholesterol
cholesterol.note: Keep saturated fat to about 6% of calories and add soluble fiber (oats, beans).

celiac.label: Celiac disease
celiac.note: Strictly gluten-free. Oats are left out unless labeled certified gluten-free.

kidney.label: Kidney disease
kidney.note: Protein, potassium and phosphorus limits depend on your stage and labs, so Handled does not set them. Ask for a renal dietitian.
kidney.confirm_with: your nephrologist or a renal dietitian

pregnancy.label: Pregnancy
pregnancy.note: No weight-loss plan during pregnancy. Avoid high-mercury fish and unpasteurized foods; take the prenatal vitamin your clinician recommends.

breastfeeding.label: Breastfeeding
breastfeeding.note: You need about 330 more calories a day in the first 6 months.
breastfeeding.confirm_with: your doctor or a lactation consultant

lactose.label: Lactose intolerance
lactose.note: Swaps: fortified soy milk and calcium-set tofu keep your calcium up.

osteoporosis.label: Osteoporosis or low bone density
osteoporosis.note: Calcium 1,200 mg and enough vitamin D; split calcium across meals.

ibs.label: IBS
ibs.note: A low-FODMAP trial can help, but it works best with a dietitian because it is temporary and strict.

eating_disorder.label: Eating disorder history
eating_disorder.note: Handled shows a balanced plate without calorie counts. If food feels hard right now, ANAD runs a free helpline.

confirm_with: your doctor or a registered dietitian
notes: Each condition carries its own source URL. Information, not medical advice. Not re-checked today.
